Question Paper  
Exam Date & Time: 23-Dec-2025 (09:30 AM - 12:30 PM)  
  
  
  MANIPAL ACADEMY OF HIGHER EDUCATION  
  FIRST SEMESTER B.TECH. DEGREE EXAMINATIONS - DEC 2025 / JAN 2026  
  SUBJECT: CSS 1001/CSS_1001 PROGRAMMING FOR PROBLEM SOLVING  
  PROGRAMMING FOR PROBLEM SOLVING [CSS 1001]  
Marks: 50                                                                                                   Duration: 180 mins.  
  
  A  
Answer all the questions.  
  
1A)               Explain the role of an operating system in managing computer hardware.                              (2)  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO1" / Cognitive Level: "Understand"  
  
1B)               Demonstrate through a flowchart and algorithm how two variables can be swapped without              (3)  
  employing a third variable.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO1" / Cognitive Level: "Understand"  
  
1C)               Design a C program that implements a digital clock using increment operators and loops.             (5)  
  Sample output:  
  00:00:00  
  00:00:01  
  00:00:02  
  ...  
  00:00:59  
  00:01:00  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO2" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
2A)               Write a C program to print all odd numbers between 50 and 100 using a while loop.                   (2)  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO2" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
2B)               i) Develop a C program to evaluate the expression                                                   (3)  
  $$result = (x++ * y-- + ++x / --y) \% (x | y);$$  
  $$ii) considering initial values of x = 5, y = 3,$$  
  Evaluate the above expression step by step, considering precedence, associativity, and evaluation  
  order.  
  (2+1 = 3 marks)  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO2" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
2C)               i) Analyze the working of the Bubble Sort algorithm with an example of sorting the array           (5)  
  [7, 3, 5, 2, 8] in ascending order. Show the array contents after each pass and mention the number  
  of comparisons and swaps made.  
  ii) Write a C program for the above situation.  
  (2+3 = 5 marks)  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO3" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
  Page #1

3A)          Explain the following string handling functions of C with proper syntax: strcpy(), strcat().           (2)  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO3" / Cognitive Level: "Understand"  
  
3B)          Write a C program to remove all other characters in a string except the alphabet. Accept the string    (3)  
  from the user.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO3" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
3C)          Define recursive function. Write a C program to check whether the given number is Armstrong or         (5)  
  not with the aid of a recursive function.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO4" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
4A)          Write a C program that demonstrates two approaches to perform a mathematical operation,             (3)  
  "incrementing a number by 5", using separate functions: one function that operates on a copy of the  
  variable and another function that modifies the original variable directly.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO4" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
4B)          Write a function to compute the sum of the first n cubes: S(n) = 1^3 + 2^3 + . . . + n^3 Print the sum (3)  
  in main() function.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO4" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
4C)          Write a C program to read M x N matrix in the main() function. Do the following tasks in function      (4)  
  called process().  
  i) Find the sum of rows and sum of columns.  
  ii) Replace all odd numbers in the matrix by binary equivalent of that number and even number by  
  least number in the matrix.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO4" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
5A)          Demonstrate different file opening modes and discuss putw() and feof() file functions with             (3)  
  appropriate syntax.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO5" / Cognitive Level: "Understand"  
  
5B)          Write a C program to find sum of all even numbers of a 1D array using a pointer to an array.           (3)  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO5" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
5C)          Develop a C program to manage bank accounts using a structure. Your program should:                   (4)  
  i) Allow the user to input the details (name, account number, account type, and balance) for multiple  
  customers.  
  ii) Provide options to read customer details, display account information, and deposit an amount into  
  a specific account.  
  iii) Implement error handling for invalid account numbers or deposit amounts.  
  iv) Ensure that the program continues to run until the user chooses to exit.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO5" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
  
  -----End-----
